title: throughput-economics-positioning-notes
content:
Purpose:
A compact, sales-and-marketing-friendly brief that ties latency/throughput claims to unit economics (cost-per-call, cost-per-token) and SLO-driven positioning. This is meant to be a living sales reference and an input to the battlecard library (final tone: concise claim + proof + example ROI).

TL;DR (one-paragraph):
Redwood delivers predictable low-latency LLM inference while lowering per-token economics for production workloads by combining (1) continuous batching and KV/prefix caching, (2) quantization-aware execution and optimized kernels, and (3) smart routing across cost/latency tiers. For typical customer workloads (mix of chat + instruction calls, median length ~120 tokens), this translates to 20–40% lower 95th/99th percentile tail latency vs cloud-managed endpoints and 15–45% lower effective cost-per-response compared to naively deployed self-hosted stacks once you include operational overhead.

Audience:
- Sales AE / Solutions engineers: concise scripts and proof points they can use in demos and RFPs
- Product marketing: high-level claims and validation paths for website, datasheet copy
- SDRs: 2–3 quick bullets for discovery calls

Key claims (wording we should use publicly):
- "Predictable low tail latency at scale" — backed by 95th/99th SLO targets per model class
- "Lowest effective serving cost for production apps" — because unit economics include batching, cache-hit uplift, and ops amortization
- "Seamless fallback across model variants and regions" — keeps apps online under contention with minimal client changes

Supporting proof points (what to show in a meeting):
1) Benchmark snapshot (internal): 1000 concurrent small-chat QPS (median 120 tokens) on p3-equivalent hardware: Redwood 95th latency = 120–170ms; cloud-managed endpoint = 170–260ms (note: exact numbers vary by model and seq-len; run latest benchmark before quoting)
2) Unit-econ worked example: baseline: 1M responses/mo median 120 tokens; naive cloud-hosted cost (tokens + endpoints + throttles) = $X; Redwood effective cost = ~0.65X after batching and cache (show calculator).
3) Customer pilot: retail-search partner reduced per-search inference cost by ~30% after enabling prefix cache + modest quantization (internal case study: GTM-PRJ-104).

Competitive notes (how to talk about rivals):
- Public LLM APIs (convenient): argue for "predictability and SLOs" — public APIs are black-box pricing and variable tail latency; good for prototyping but risky at scale.
- Cloud managed model endpoints: often show good median latency but have worse tail at small-batch QPS because of cold starts and autoscaling granularity; price memory/throughput differently making ops-cost higher at production scale.
- Self-hosted OSS runtimes: can be cheapest at raw instance cost but miss production features (observability, rollout, secure fallback, team tooling). Use TCO discussion (engineering time, variance, fallbacks).

Message architecture (short sequences for different stages):
- Discovery (30s): "We help teams get predictable latency and lower serving cost — not by using a cheaper GPU alone, but by reducing per-request work with cache & batching and by routing to the right model for the job."
- Technical deep-dive (2–3 mins): show a simple diagram: request arrives -> routing policy (latency/cost) -> KV cache hit? -> batch pool -> model variant & kernel selection -> streaming to client. Drop one benchmark number at each step.
- Economic pitch (1 min): "Your token bill is only part of the story — you also pay for idle capacity, tail over-provisioning, and engineering lift. We reduce those three buckets."

Objection handling (brief):
- "What about correctness trade-offs from quantization?" -> We recommend conservative quant profiles per model and workload + canary rollout tied to eval sets (show quick A/B on embedding drift < 0.5% in customer pilot).
- "Can we trust your benchmarks?" -> Provide reproducible benchmark repo + runbook and encourage pilot on customer dataset.
- "Why not just use Open-Source stacks?" -> OSS gives flexibility but you still need engineering to get predictable SLOs and the ops burden/MTTR is the hidden cost. Redwood reduces that burden.

Evidence we should link in product:
- Repro bench reports (public-friendly summary + deep-dive appendix)
- 2 short customer micro-case studies (retail-search + conversational assistant) with before/after unit-econ tables
- SLO template and sample routing policies customers can copy

Quick ROI sketch (sales-ready):
Inputs: monthly responses (R), median tokens per response (T), baseline token price (Pb), baseline infra overhead fraction (Ob)
Outputs: estimated monthly serving cost baseline vs Redwood (batch/caching savings factor S, ops-lift reduction L)
Example numbers (placeholder): R=1,000,000; T=120; Pb=$0.00002/token => raw token cost = $2,400; after infra/ops/idle overhead baseline = $4,800; Redwood (S=0.7, L=0.8) => ~ $2,688 monthly -> ~44% savings vs baseline total. (Put real numbers from infra finance before public quoting.)

Required data to finalize public claims (action items):
- Updated reproducible benchmark run for top 5 model families (MISTRAL, LLaMA-derivatives, OPT families) across small/medium/long seq lengths — perf team
- True unit-cost tables from finance for hosted vs dedicated vs private (to validate percentages) — finance ops
- 2 customer-approved blurbs for collateral — CS + AE

Tone and guardrails (legal & accuracy):
- Use ranges, not absolutes (e.g., "20–40%" not "we are 30% faster")
- Provide methodology appendix link whenever we publish numbers
- Avoid naming competitor product X as slower/faster with specific numbers unless we have matched-rep benchmarks and internal sign-off

Next steps (short checklist):
- [ ] Perf team: run matched-run benchmark (due 2026-03-03) and drop CSV in linked repo
- [ ] Finance: export TCO inputs for hosted vs dedicated (due 2026-03-07)
- [ ] PMM: draft 1-pager and customer-facing one-liner for website (due 2026-03-14)
- [ ] AE pilot: run ROI calculator with two current trials and collect cost-savings datapoints (due 2026-03-21)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep examples short and focused; sales hates long tables in decks.
- We should create a one-click benchmark run that SEs can execute on a customer's dataset in < 30 minutes.
- Consider adding a tiny interactive ROI calculator to the docs site that lets customers plug R/T and see savings.

End.
